title: kiln-baked, crunchy malaysian cookies bowl
description: show off your culinary skills with this sweet and crunchy malaysian dish featuring kiln-baked cookies, flambe, and presented in a traditional dolsot-stone-bowl
instructions: Preheat your kiln to 375 degrees fahrenheit and place the dolsot stone-bowl inside for 30 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the almond flour, granulated sugar, unsalted butter, large eggs, vanilla extract, and sugar cookie mix. Mix well until a smooth dough forms.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the coconut milk and coconut oil.
Gradually add the coconut milk mixture to the dough and mix until a sticky ball forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and pliable.
Place the dough on a lightly floured surface and roll it out to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Cut the dough into desired shapes using a cookie cutter.
Place the cut cookies on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 15-20 minutes or until the edges are golden brown.
Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
In a small saucepan, heat the dark chocolate chips over low heat, stirring occasionally, until melted and smooth.
To assemble the dish, place 4-6 cookies in the dolsot stone-bowl, drizzle with melted dark chocolate, and sprinkle with hulled sesame seeds and cinnamon powder.
Place the bowl under the broiler for 30 seconds to caramelize the sugar and melt the chocolate.
Remove the bowl from the oven and let it cool for 1 minute before serving.
